messages:
maria: noticing regressions on prod console after last rollout, sparklines and heatmap panels stall ~400-800ms on nav. LCP on /org/*/dashboard up ~0.7s. not consistent but correlated to certain orgs with huge metric sets.
alex: which rollout? can you paste canary id and bundle version?
paul: deploy-bot: deploy v2.16.0-canary.3 -> console (by @paul) at 2026-03-22T11:02:30Z
maria: that's the one. trace attached from a repro run (quick scroll):
```
main: parseJSON -> hydrateRows -> renderHeatmap -> computeBuckets
cpu: spike in computeBuckets, also network stall on /kv/prefix/hydrate
```
jin: hmm we flipped route-policy to "route-by-tenant" + async prefetch for those tables last week. Could be cache shard skew causing prefix misses and extra back-and-forth.
sam: telemetry: noticed a 3x increase in prefix-miss rate for kv-store from 03:00 to 04:00 UTC matching canary window. spike in rpc tail latency too. link: https://telemetry.internal/q/trace/abc123
alex: we also shipped client-side aggregation to reduce server cost (bundle delta +15kb). client agg runs on main thread and uses a WebWorker fallback only if available. on some browsers worker creation is throttled -> main thread takes the hit.
maria: so two orthogonal changes aligning: routing -> cache misses -> increased network waits; and client agg -> compute on main thread. combined = perceived jank.
paul: short term options: A) rollback route-by-tenant routing for console traffic, B) disable client-side agg or force worker usage, C) enable aggressive prefetch + local LRU to mask misses.
ops-bot: current canary traffic ~8%. rollback window ends in 45m.
alex: I'll push a tiny patch to the canary: set kv-affinity=legacy for console route header + feature-flag client-agg=off for canary clients. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/console/merge/4389
jin: I'll add a staging regression that simulates shard-reshuffle and monitors prefix-miss ratio and main-thread-block ms per route. also adding a telemetry alert: kv.prefix_miss_rate > 4% for 1m -> page-performance channel.
sam: also recommend we add an observability metric: per-route worker-creation-fallback-rate so we can see how often client agg falls back to main thread.
maria: after patch lands canary 2 will run at 11:30 UTC. I will validate using large org dashboard and paste screenshots. if green we can roll forward. can we also gate client-agg behind rollout UX so that console sees staged client binaries?
alex: good call. we'll gate via rollout tag and add rollout-ui opt-in in console settings to test for engs.
paul: rolling patch now. will update here with canary results. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — pinging @ops for help if rollback needed.
ops-bot: noted. I'll be ready to roll back route changes if telemetry doesn't improve.
paul: canary 2 scheduled and running. will post trace snapshots in ~10m.
maria: saw initial improvement in LCP ~ -0.4s in canary 2. still validating scroll stutter but looks promising. will post final numbers in 15m.
